Header:
Date: 2026-06-09
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (BrightLayer), Daniel Cho (BrightLayer), Leah Ng (BrightLayer)
Shared artifacts: latency heatmap (drive), pilot metrics sheet: https://redwood.ai/pilot/brightlayer/metrics-sheet

Summary:
Weekly POC sync to review model selection signals, pinning strategy, fallback simulations from the staging runs, and decide next safety tabletop. Tradeoffs discussed: latency spikes vs unit cost, quantization quality, KV cache warmup behavior.

Topics:
- Catalog delta: v1.3-small vs v2.0-med (quantized)
- Rollback and soft-fallback playbook
- Heatmap and tail-latency outliers
- Compliance gating and log retention for pilot

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, um this is our weekly sync for the BrightLayer pilot. we'll start with a quick recap of results and then go into the fallback sims. Priya, you wanna kick us off with the heatmap?
[00:27] Priya: yeah sure, so I pulled the staging runs from last thursday, the 8-bit and 4-bit quant runs. main delta — v2.0-med quantized at 8-bit gave us about 12% cost savings but latency tail increased for longer contexts, especially at 1k tokens. KV cache warmup was fine for repeated sessions but new-session cold starts show a 220 to 320 ms bump.
[00:55] Marta: sorry can you explain the KV cache warmup thing one more time? is that with our conversational session pattern?
[01:03] Priya: yeah, so because you are doing multi-turn with user history, the KV cache is building; on cold nodes the first few requests have to pay the cache populate cost. we see the head tokens are normal but the p99 moves.
[01:18] Daniel: does that mean we should bias toward smaller model for first turn then swap up? is that possible?
[01:25] Priya: technically yes, that's a router pattern — start with v1.3-small for new session, then promote to v2.0-med as cache warms. Redwood can do that with a two-step routing policy or a warmup flag. we ran a soft-fallback simulation where requests that hit >250ms go to the smaller model.
[01:45] Leah: did you see any quality regressions when we move to 8-bit? especially on clinical summarization prompts?
[01:52] Priya: good callout — on our summary eval set there was a small drop in ROUGE-L for a subset of templates, about -1.8 points, and a handful of hallucination cases in the 4-bit runs. 8-bit looked acceptable for most intents, but the clinical template with lots of numeric tables degraded more.
[02:14] Alex: okay so tradeoff matrix — cost saved vs small QoR drop and occasional hallucination. My question to BrightLayer is what are your strict thresholds for quality delta? when is a rollback mandatory?
[02:28] Marta: for production we need zero hallucination on discharge summary and anything that goes to downstream billing has to be within 0.5% error — for the pilot we're comfortable with a small -1 ROUGE if we can flag and human-in-the-loop the risky ones.
[02:44] Alex: good, that clarifies a rollback policy: automatic rollback if hallucination rate > 0.4% on monitored prompts, otherwise soft-fallback. we'll document that.
[02:55] Daniel: on routing — what about cost spikes during peak usage? if the smaller model is overloaded will Redwood route to region fallback or queue?
[03:05] Priya: Redwood routing supports policy layers: primary model, variant pool, then region fallback. we've simulated a region failure and the platform will fall back to cross-region nodes which increases latency but keeps throughput. we also have a circuit-breaker that rejects low-priority ops.
[03:19] Speaker 1: (mumble) how about audit logs and retention for the pilot?
[03:23] Alex: good reminder — Marta, you asked about compliance. for pilot, we can enable audit logs with 90-day retention; if you need SOC2 artifacts we can share our SOC2 binder but for Private you'd want on-prem/KMS.
[03:36] Marta: we'll review that with legal. for now 90 days is fine.
[03:40] Priya: back to the fallback sim — we ran 10k synthetic sessions with a 15% cold-start rate; the soft-fallback rule dropped p99 from 820 ms to 540 ms for the tail, cost increased slightly because of duplication during promotion, but overall token cost was down ~7% vs always-on v2.0-med.
[04:03] Leah: can we get those synthetic sessions aligned to our real distribution? earlier runs used uniform length, we need more >800 token cases to stress the tails.
[04:13] Priya: yes I can re-generate with the distribution from your logs — I need that export.
[04:17] Daniel: I can share yesterday's session histogram by EOD.
[04:20] Alex: perfect. On pinning — we propose pinning v2.0-med as default for 80% traffic, v1.3-small as fallback, and a canary v2.1-alpha at 1% for nightly integration tests. Priya, is 1% enough to catch regressions?
[04:36] Priya: it depends on the signal. for hallucination it's low sample; I'd recommend adding targeted prompts in the canary set so we exercise the failure modes. we also recommend model gating: automatic rollback on elevated hallucination confidence.
[04:49] Marta: how do we surface hallucination confidence? do you have detectors or do we rely on our classifiers?
[04:55] Priya: Redwood has a built-in reranker/quality-check hook that runs a lightweight hallucination detector. it's not perfect, but we can also plumb your classifier into the eval pipeline.
[05:05] Alex: action item — Priya add the hallucination detector hook into staging and run it against the canary.
[05:10] Priya: noted.
[05:12] Alex: any blockers on the rollback playbook?
[05:15] Daniel: one note — our infra team wants a dry-run of the emergency rollback; if we flip traffic back to v1.3 we'll need to ensure capacity is standing by. what does 'standing by' mean in Redwood? reserved instances or instant spin-up?
[05:29] Priya: for Dedicated you'd have reserved capacity; for Hosted we have pre-warmed pools and rapid warm start but there is a brief period of throughput hiccup. because this is a pilot on Hosted, plan for a 3–5 minute runway to scale up the smaller variant. we can reduce that to under 2 minutes if we pre-warm a minimal pool.
[05:45] Marta: can you quantify cost of pre-warming? we need to compare to risk of a problematic rollback.
[05:50] Alex: yes I'll add pre-warm cost to the benchmarking sheet.
[05:54] Leah: quick question about model metadata — when we pin should we record quantization profile and tokenizer version? we had a mismatch in a previous run.
[06:02] Priya: absolutely, pin should include model hash, quant profile, tokenizer id, and runtime kernel set. Redwood's model catalog supports those fields in the pin.
[06:12] Alex: cool. Last section — tabletop drill scheduling. propose week of 2026-06-22, 45 minute drill with SE, infra, product, and legal on call.
[06:24] Marta: works for us.
[06:26] Alex: recap of next steps: Alex send heatmap+csv, Priya run extra quant runs and add hallucination hook, Marta confirm compliance items, Daniel share histograms. we'll reconvene next Tuesday same time.
[06:40] (end of recording)
